title: Model pin journey - comparison cards, preview diff wires and microcopy experiments
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures wireframe annotations and microcopy experiments for a compact ‘model pin journey’ in the catalog and endpoint create flows. Focus: comparison-card UX to choose a model version, preview-diff modal (what changes when you pin), and safe rollback / progressive-rollout wording.

Context and user problems we’re solving:
- Users need to pick a model version for an endpoint quickly while understanding behavioral deltas between versions (latency/cost/quality).
- Pinning should be reversible and auditable; users must feel safe doing it.
- In endpoint creation, the friction of version selection should be low — show a compact comparison and a quick preview rather than a full settings page.

High-level flow sketches (wireframe intent, not final art):
1) Catalog list -> compact comparison card group (3-up horizontal on wide screens, stacked on mobile). Each card includes: version badge, short changelog 1-2 lines, tokens/latency estimate, quant/precision tag, and a visual dot for recent regressions. CTA: “Select & preview”.
2) Select & preview opens a lightweight slide-over with two panes: LEFT: live example prompt and recent request trace (sample outputs for both versions). RIGHT: side-by-side metric snapshot (avg latency, 95p, cost/token, failure rate). Top of slide-over: banner: “Preview only — nothing is changed until you confirm pin.”
3) Confirm pin modal: shows rollout options: Immediate, Canary (% slider with presets 5/20/50), and Scheduled. Small help text under slider: “Start small to validate quality, Redwood will route and collect quality metrics for 24h before recommending full rollout.”
4) Post-pin toast & changelog entry: toast copy + link to rollout page. Endpoint page shows a pinned-version chip with hover tooltip: timestamp, pinned-by, changelog excerpt, and rollback link.

Microcopy experiments (examples to A/B test):
- Card CTA options: A) “Select & preview” B) “Try this version” C) “Compare”
- Preview banner: A) “This is a preview — you aren’t changing traffic.” B) “Previewing outputs for v1.11 — pin only when ready.”
- Confirm modal heading: A) “Pin model version to endpoint” B) “Lock this version to the endpoint” (hypothesis: “lock” implies stronger immutability; may increase caution)
- Rollout slider label options: A) “Canary traffic” B) “Traffic percent” C) “Gradual rollout”
- Rollout help text options (short): A) “Redwood collects quality signals and will show regressions in 24h.” B) “Start at a low percent, check evals, then increase.”
- Success toast options: A) “Pinned v1.11 — tracking quality for 24h. View rollout.” B) “Pinned — changes active for selected traffic. See details.”
- Rollback CTA: A) “Rollback to previous version” B) “Revert pin” C) “Restore prior model”

Edge cases and error states to cover in wires and copy: 
- Model has no prior versions (empty state): content suggestions: header: “No version history yet” body: “This model has a single uploaded version. You can pin it now or upload a new build to compare.” Buttons: “Pin current version” and “Upload new version”.
- Pin conflict (two concurrent pin attempts): banner: “A pin is in progress by Diego Martinez. You can watch the rollout or request control.” Buttons: “Watch rollout” and “Request override” (override should open a modal with required justification and audit log entry).
- Canary shows regression: inline banner in endpoint: “Quality alert — 5% traffic shows higher hallucination rate compared to baseline. Pause rollout?” Buttons: “Pause” / “View failing prompts” / “Increase sample size”. Copy should avoid alarmist language, focus on actionable next steps.
- Insufficient permissions: “You need deploy permissions to pin a version. Contact your org admin or request access.” Provide link to invite flow.

Accessibility & truncation rules for cards: 
- Version badge should include ARIA label with full semantic version and commit SHA (short).
- Changelog: show up to two lines with “...more” link that opens full changelog in slide-over.

Telemetry & observability requirements (notes for SRE/product): 
- Events to emit: pin_initiated, pin_confirmed, rollout_step (percent change), pin_rolled_back, pin_override_requested. Each should include user id, endpoint id, model id, previous_version, new_version, and reason (optional).
- UI should surface last 7 days of eval comparisons in preview modal (histograms + example outputs).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Compact comparison cards in catalog list (desktop and mobile responsive) with working Select & preview flow.
- Preview slide-over shows sample outputs and metric snapshot for two selected versions.
- Confirm modal supports immediate and canary rollouts (percent slider with presets).
- Pin appears on endpoint page with pinned-version chip and rollback action.
- Telemetry events fired for pin actions.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Copy: prefer ‘Pin’ vs ‘Lock’ vs ‘Freeze’? (Product leaning towards ‘Pin’ to match existing language but explore user test.)
- Should the preview show deterministic sample outputs (same prompt for both versions) or user’s actual recent requests? (Privacy + reproducibility concerns)
- How long should Redwood automatically monitor a canary before suggesting full rollout? 24h is baseline — validate with SRE.

Next steps / owner assignments:
- Design: polish comparison-card anatomy and provide Figma frames for desktop/mobile (owner: Diego Martinez) — due 2024-10-18.
- PM: finalize copy variants for user testing and pick primary/secondary options (owner: Samantha Chen) — due 2024-10-11.
- Eng: draft telemetry schema and decide on rollout guardrails (owner: Asha Patel) — due 2024-11-01.

Notes to reviewers (quick reading guide):
- Scroll to the microcopy experiments if you want to give quick feedback on tone.
- Check the edge cases section to confirm we captured your experience needs (especially security and multi-admin conflicts).

Rough mock copy fragments you can paste into Figma: 
- Card subtitle: “v1.11 • quantized int8 • 20% faster • +small-context-fix”
- Card body (changelog): “Fix: reduced trailing hallucination on product-descriptions; Perf: median latency down 18%”
- Preview banner: “Previewing outputs for v1.11 — safe sandbox”
- Confirm modal primary CTA: “Pin version and start rollout”
- Canary helper: “Start with a small canary to verify output quality before full migration.”
- Rollback prompt: “Rolling back will reroute traffic immediately. Select a version to restore.”

Changelog for this doc (quick history):
- 2024-10-02: created (initial sketch and microcopy ideas)
- 2024-10-16: added edge cases and telemetry notes after sync with SRE
- 2024-11-21: updated acceptance criteria and next steps after design grooming

Please add comments inline in Figma and add any sample failing prompts to the linked Confluence page.
